notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg0527.tlg033.1st1K-gr: ἡγοῦυτο χείραω (18.6.4) is a misprint, read as ἡγοῦντο χείρω, 'they judged worse'.
ἰδιότητος, 'his own proper being'; the variant ἀιδιότητος would give 'his own eternity'. In 2:24 'it' takes αὐτόν as death.

nodes.text: nor did they hope for the wages of holiness,
nor did they discern the reward of blameless souls.
For God created man for incorruption,
and made him an image of his own proper being;
but through the envy of the devil death entered into the world,
and those who belong to his portion experience it.
But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God,
the natures of living creatures and the tempers of wild beasts,
the violent forces of winds and the reasonings of men,
the varieties of plants and the powers of roots;
and all things that are hidden or manifest I came to know,
for Wisdom, the craftswoman of all things, taught me.
so that, freed from wickedness, they may believe in you, Lord.
For the ancient inhabitants of your holy land, too,
you hated for practising most hateful works of sorcery
and unholy rites,
and merciless murderers of children,
And in their terror, worse than that sight which was not seen
they judged the things they saw.
And the tricks of the magic art lay prostrate,
and their boast of wisdom met with a disgraceful refutation;
for those who promised to drive away terrors and disturbances from a soul
that was sick,
these were sick with a ridiculous fear.
